items.excerpt: Google Ads We’re bringing AI Brief to more languages and adding a new AI Max reporting feature. Sep 23, 2026 We’re rolling out new AI Max features that provide advertisers with greater control and new reporting to understand performance. First, we’re bringing the closed beta of AI Brief to more languages: Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish. AI Brief lets you guide AI Max in your own words with detailed context on your business, audience, and key messaging. Second, we’re introducing a new reporting feature in Google Ads to give you a clearer view of AI-driven performance. It will show a single, unified view of the Search ads journey — making it easy to see what search terms triggered your ads, which creative assets the user saw, and exactly where they landed on your website. This precise interface will help you better understand how customers interact with your business and validate the strategic value AI Max brings to your campaigns. We’ll share additional details and availability later this year.

items.excerpt: AI is coming to ChatGPT ads… When creating a ChatGPT ads campaign, some advertisers are seeing this new toggle: Text Customization. Let’s take a closer look… What Is It? It’s on by default, and it reads: AI automatically generates personalized and translated versions of your ad’s headlines and descriptions, which may be shown without your individual review or approval. It’s interesting that OpenAI is making AI enhancements a priority for their beta ads product. Similar enhancements are the target of the most common complaints from Meta advertisers. But if you hoped to escape this with ChatGPT ads, you’d be mistaken. How Does It Work? What’s crazy is how mysterious OpenAI makes this. What would personalized versions of headlines and descriptions look like? We won’t know because there aren’t any more details or previews. And you won’t have the opportunity to review and approve those changes ahead of time. Of course, you can just globally turn these off for now, but you’ll need to do it with each campaign.

items.excerpt: As Meta advertising continues to evolve, a segment of advertisers gets left behind. They’re stuck in the old ways of doing things, determined to control things that no longer need to be controlled. But they have every right to be confused. I’m not saying that you should use the broadest targeting with Advantage+ Placements in every case. You should prioritize a hands-off approach, but there are exceptions when some control is necessary. How you exert that control is important. This post will focus on how to approach control for the following elements: Age Gender Custom audiences (remarketing) Detailed targeting and lookalike audiences Placements Let’s take a closer look… 1. Age Primary Approach: Hands Off or Suggestions If you’re optimizing for a purchase or conversion of some kind, avoid making initial adjustments to age. Resist the urge to restrict by age to reflect your target customer. While I would generally start without any targeting inputs for age, audience suggestions won’t hurt. If you want to use suggestions, go ahead. I’ve generally found that such suggestions make no impact at all . If Meta can find optimized results from an age group outside of your suggested range,…

items.excerpt: You can turn off the new creative workflow… Meta started rolling out the new creative workflow in April. Also known as Multimedia Experience, it allows advertisers to provide up to 10 images and videos for a single ad. While I use and have generally been happy with the Multimedia Experience, I know I’m in the minority. Most advertisers hate it, mainly because it’s so buggy. Advertisers have had bugs both with ad creation and reporting using the breakdown by Media. What most of these advertisers don’t understand is that you don’t need to keep dealing with these bugs. You can turn this off and switch to the old way. How to Turn It Off When creating an ad, hover over the Media tooltip. There, you can click a link to “Return to original single media experience.” Even if you switch to single media, you can always hover over the same tooltip to switch back to multimedia if you want to in the future. Switch While You Can Presumably, you won’t be able to do this once the Multimedia Experience is officially launched, but you have an option for now. If you’re experiencing so many bugs that it’s not worth it, just switch back.

Here are some resources to help you with the migration: Upgrade to the newest version Release notes To view a list of methods and services that your project has recently called, use the Google Cloud Console : Open APIs & Services in the Google Cloud Console. Click Google Ads API in the table. On the Metrics subtab, your recent requests are plotted on each graph. You can see which methods you've sent requests to in the Methods table. The method name includes a Google Ads API version, a service, and a method name, such as google.ads.googleads.v22.services.GoogleAdsService.Mutate . (Optional) Select the timeframe for which you want to view your requests. If you have any questions or want to discuss this post, reach out to Google Ads API support or start a discussion on our “Google Advertising and Measurement Community” Discord server . - Ben Karl, on behalf of the Google Ads API Team

In this Ads Decoded episode, Ginny Marvin, Ads Product Liaison, sits down with John Chen, Senior Director of Product Management for Ads Measurement, to cut through the noise. They discuss building a measurement stack across attribution, incrementality, and MMM, capturing longer purchase journeys with Qualified Future Conversions, and why treating media spend like planting seeds beats short-term ROAS (return on ad spend) chasing. And in a bonus episode, Patrick Gilbert and Nechama Teigman from AdVenture Media give an unvarnished look at implementing Meridian, Google’s open-source MMM. Discover how AI coding tools erase technical barriers, why data variance matters more than budget size, and how to plan your next strategic test. Watch the full episode here and the companion episode here .

items.excerpt: Advertisers have spotted a new Automatic Events option in the Settings tab of Events Manager. If you’re a good Meta advertiser who pays attention, this should look at least vaguely familiar to you. There is an old feature that’s described in almost the same way. I assure you there are differences. But if you’re confused, you’d be forgiven. Based on what I’ve been able to sort out, Meta’s made some administrative errors that make this far more confusing than it needs to be. Let’s break it down… The Old Feature As I mentioned at the top, the concept of Automatic Events may sound familiar to you because Meta introduced something very similar four years ago. This “Track Events Automatically Without Code” feature was originally found immediately below the Event Setup Tool within the Settings tab of Events Manager. Here’s how Meta described it: Your Meta Pixel can find and report on valuable website events, such as purchases or registrations, based on your site traffic, button text and page metadata. This feature can help you set up events without having to install code. You can choose to turn this functionality on or off. The New Feature The new Automatic Events feature is also found…

items.excerpt: We are updating our Google Ads Developer Policies formerly the “Google Ads API Policy”, to support developers in building robust, high-quality integrations as new AI capabilities continue to shape the advertising industry. These updates establish clear frameworks for emerging technologies that are more secure and drive better outcomes for our shared customers. To ensure a seamless transition to these updated standards, the Ads API Compliance team is actively reviewing existing integrations. items.excerpt: What’s going on here? Meta introduced Customer Lifecycle Strategy a few months ago. It allows you to define whether you want to get conversions from all audiences or only acquire new customers. When you choose to acquire new customers, you’ll need to define the custom audiences you want to exclude. But Meta is doing something weird now, and you need to be careful. Custom Audiences Automatically Excluded Immediately after selecting to acquire new customers, I can see that custom audiences are already being excluded. When I click to edit the excluded audiences, I see that several custom audiences already appear for Existing Customers. These weren’t custom audiences I manually selected. Meta attempted to predict which audiences I’d want to exclude, and it’s not even close. Not only is the list incomplete, but it includes audiences that do not match my existing customers. For what it’s worth, Meta didn’t try to do this with my engaged audience. That field was left blank. So just know that if you only want to acquire new customers, you’ll need to go through these manually. Otherwise, you’re likely to exclude the wrong audiences. We’re making Demand Gen ads even more relevant for travelers by surfacing local activities, events, and real-time offers. We're also personalizing hotel ads to show relevant properties to the right audiences. We’re making Multimodal Video Creation in Asset Studio generally available. Advertisers can now go from storyboarding to creating horizontal and vertical assets in one workflow, enabling them to show up across all Demand Gen inventory. Ready to rethink your performance marketing approach? Join us for Rethink Week 2026 and get started with The YouTube Performance Four today.

items.excerpt: A major release of the Google Ads API Developer Assistant is now available. This release transitions the assistant from a standalone project setup to a unified plugin architecture designed to bring specialized Google Ads API capabilities directly into AI agent workflows. What is it? The Google Ads API Developer Assistant brings deep Google Ads domain expertise into AI coding environments like Antigravity and Claude Code. It equips your AI assistant with specialized tools and guardrails. Functions include: Generate idiomatic code : Create tested, best-practice integration code across Python, Java, PHP, .NET, and Ruby. Validate GAQL queries : Automatically verifies syntax, field compatibility, date segmentation, and zero-impression rules before running queries. Inspect Protobuf schemas : On demand discovery of resource fields, data types, and enum definitions for any active Google Ads API version to ensure that GAQL query fields are valid. Troubleshoot API issues : Diagnose offline conversion upload failures, navigate manager account hierarchies, and construct Performance Max listing filters.
